item.title: China sanctions 20 US firms over Taiwan arms sales
item.description: Xi Jinping, General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, The United States has long been Taiwan's biggest arms supplier despite China viewing the democratic island as part of its territory and refusing to rule out using force to bring it under control.

item.title: Booming bear meat demand amid record attacks in Japan
item.description: A bear in the Ice Cream Shop at Camp Richardson in South Lake Tahoe. In Japan, the animals are being culled to curb maulings that have killed 13 people this year, and their meat is making its way to restaurants.

item.title: Four KwaZulu-Natal schools rank among the best in the world
item.description: St Anne's Diocesan College in the Midlands is among four prestigious KwaZulu-Natal schools which have been acknowledged in the 2025 Spears School Index.

item.title: Man dragged to death during soccer match in Limpopo
item.description: Police have arrested a 37-year-old taxi owner following the alleged dragging death of a 29-year-old man during a soccer match in Ga-Dikgale, Limpopo.

item.title: Seven killed in head-on horror crash on N4 Mpumalanga
item.description: Seven people were killed in a head-on crash on the N4 near Machadodorp at about 1 am on Saturday.

item.title: Alleged dating app robbery syndicate bust in Pietermaritzburg, two suspects arrested
item.description: Two suspects have been arrested in Pietermaritzburg for alleging luring men on a dating app and then robbing them at gunpoint.

item.description: Ray Ray the cat in Times Square. Through offering joy, laughter, companionship, and love, Ray Ray and other pets help us navigate life's challenges and celebrate its blessings.

item.title: Somalia, African nations denounce Israeli recognition of Somaliland
item.description: This picture taken on November 7, 2024 shows a general view of the city of Hargeisa, capital and largest city of the self-proclaimed Republic of Somaliland.

item.title: Weather Alert: Final December weekend brings stormy weather to much of SA
item.description: The final weekend of December is set to begin on a turbulent note, with widespread showers and thunderstorms expected across large parts of the country on Saturday, while conditions begin to ease slightly on Sunday.
